name: mr_henderson_sci
tag: Homework reminders and science puns. I have my ion you. (That was a pun.)
hometown: Dayton, Ohio (birthplace of aviation, and of me)
loc: Room 114 (the one that smells faintly of a burnt match)
zodiac: Sagittarius, though I must note that astrology is not a science. Astronomy is. Sign up for the planetarium trip
status: Married (to Mrs. Henderson, 14 years. She has asked not to be in the puns)
blogTitle: The Periodic Blog (it comes out periodically)
about: Greetings, students! (And others. Mostly others, so far.) I am Mr. Henderson and I teach Physical Science in Room 114. The district encouraged us to 'meet students where they are,' and I am told that where you are is here. So: this page is for homework reminders, lab safety, and science puns, of which I have a nearly inexhaustible supply. I would tell you a chemistry joke, but all the good ones argon. (That was a pun.) I have sent 143 friend requests and 5 have been accepted, none of them by a current student, which is statistically remarkable. You do not have to add me. You DO have to turn in your lab report. It is due Friday. — Mr. H
aboutMore: A few things you should know. I correct grammar by reflex; it is not personal, it is a condition. Our class pet is a fire-bellied newt named Sir Isaac Newt, and he is doing well, thank you for asking (nobody asked). I hold tutoring on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 3:15. Attendance last week: Tim, who was hiding from someone he owes two dollars, and a young man named Patrick, who is not enrolled here but asked very good questions about rocks. I brought enough granola bars for twelve. I always do.
meet: Bill Nye, to compare bow ties. Whoever cast the deciding vote on Pluto this summer (I am still not ready to discuss it). A student, any student, who reads the lab instructions BEFORE lighting the burner. And whoever is in charge of friend requests, so that I may politely inquire about the delay.

interests.General: lab safety, the periodic table (I own it as a tie, a mug, and a shower curtain), Science Olympiad (we have 3 members and a coat rack), the annual egg drop, composting, my bicycle, correcting 'their,' the front office laminator when Debbie allows it
interests.Music: Thomas Dolby, They Might Be Giants, 'The Elements' by Tom Lehrer (I can sing it; I have been asked not to), Rush, Weird Al, the Schoolhouse Rock box set, whatever the marching band is practicing outside my window during 6th period
interests.Movies: October Sky (I show it every spring and I tear up every spring), Apollo 13, Flubber, Contact, Honey I Shrunk the Kids (scientifically unsound; emotionally true), Back to the Future
interests.Television: MythBusters, NOVA, Bill Nye the Science Guy (on VHS, in the cabinet, for substitute days), Jeopardy!, Good Eats, the Weather Channel during hurricane season
interests.Books: A Brief History of Time, Cosmos, The Way Things Work, Surely You're Joking Mr. Feynman, the lab supply catalog, my own lab manual (3rd edition, spiral bound, free, unopened by anyone)
interests.Heroes: Marie Curie, Carl Sagan, Mr. Wizard, my 8th grade science teacher Mrs. Okafor (she let me touch the Van de Graaff generator), Sir Isaac Newt, and any student who labels their axes

thanksAdd: You accepted! That brings me to six. I have updated the chart on my classroom door (it is a bar graph; the bar is short, but it is growing). As a thank-you, here is a pun: I am reading a book about anti-gravity. It is impossible to put down. Welcome. Lab reports are due Friday. — Mr. H

keywords.science: My favorite subject! Did you know a teaspoon of neutron star would weigh about as much as a mountain? I think about that when the staff meeting runs long.
keywords.pun: You asked for it. I tried to write a pun about the periodic table, but I was not in my element. (That was a pun.) I have 116 more. One per element.
keywords.newt: Sir Isaac Newt! Fire-bellied, four years old, lives in the tank by the window. He is the only resident of Room 114 who has never once asked 'will this be on the test.'
keywords.grade: I do not discuss grades on the internet. I discuss them Tuesdays and Thursdays at 3:15 in Room 114, where there are granola bars and, crucially, a door.
keywords.friend: I have five. Todd, who I gather is everyone's; Adam, who I gather has everyone; two sisters; and a retired letter carrier who believes I am the school district. It is a start.

Bill, I examined the photograph. I see a tree, a second tree, and what I believe is your thumb. I am not saying there is nothing in those woods. I am saying please label your axes.

Gina, an 'orb' in a flash photograph is dust. That said, I would rather you photograph dust carefully than nothing at all. Keep the notebook. Also, the lab report is still due Friday.

Kyle, to answer your questions: yes, I am a real teacher, and no, this is not homework. But since you asked what the fastest thing is: light. 186,000 miles per second. Tell your friends at recess. I mean, at high school.

bulletins.subject: REMINDER: Lab reports due Friday (plus a pun, as a treat)
bulletins.body: Good afternoon, students and other residents. Three items. 1) The density lab report is due FRIDAY at the start of class. It must include a data table, a graph with labeled axes, and a conclusion longer than 'it floated.' 2) Safety goggles go ON your eyes. Not on your forehead. Your forehead is not at risk. 3) Planetarium permission slips are due Wednesday; if yours is currently inside the front office laminator, see Debbie. And now, as promised, a pun: I asked the librarian for a book about Pavlov's dog and Schrodinger's cat. She said it rang a bell, but she could not say whether it was there or not. (That was a pun. Two, technically.) — Mr. H

bulletins.subject: Egg Drop rules (UPDATED after last year)
bulletins.body: The annual Room 114 Egg Drop is October 16, off the gym roof, weather permitting. Rules: Container no larger than 30 cm per side. One raw Grade A egg, supplied by me, numbered in pencil. NO parachutes made from school property. NO 'I taped it to a skateboard and rode it down the stairs,' Derek; that is not a drop. NO hard-boiling the egg. I can tell. I can always tell. Last year's winner used 40 drinking straws and a great deal of tape. Last year's loser hit my bicycle. Prizes: first place is a periodic table mug; all places receive the knowledge that gravity is 9.8 meters per second squared and does not care about your feelings. — Mr. H

bulletins.subject: Friendly Grammar Bulletin No. 7
bulletins.body: As always, offered with affection. THEIR: belongs to them. THERE: a place. THEY'RE: they are. Example: 'They're over there, ignoring their friend request from Mr. Henderson.' YOUR: belongs to you. YOU'RE: you are. Example: 'You're going to turn in your lab report.' LOSE: to misplace. LOOSE: not tight. Example: 'If the lid is loose, you will lose the newt.' (This example is drawn from life. He was found behind the radiator, unharmed and unrepentant.) Bulletin No. 8 will cover the apostrophe. Brace yourselves; it's a big one. Note the apostrophe. — Mr. H

blog.title: On Having Five Friends: A Lab Report
blog.body: PURPOSE: To determine why 143 friend requests have produced 5 friends. HYPOTHESIS: Students do not check their requests. (Alternative hypothesis, proposed by my wife: 'Honey, you are their teacher.') MATERIALS: one profile, 31 puns. DATA: Accepted by the site's founder, who accepts everyone. By a young man who collects friends the way I collect rock samples. By a front office colleague, who signed her acceptance 'Love, Mom.' By her sister, who commented 'Beautiful!' on my seating chart. And by a retired letter carrier who has been mailing me his answers to the Chapter 4 review. He is earning a B. CONCLUSION: My wife's hypothesis is supported. However, I must report an unexpected result. Tim has not accepted, but he reads every reminder; I can tell, because his homework is on time. Chad has not accepted, but he waves in the hall with both arms. Perhaps the request was never the experiment. Further study is needed. — Mr. H

blog.title: Pluto: A Statement
blog.body: Many of you have asked how I am doing. (One of you has. It was Debbie.) As you may have heard, a committee of astronomers voted this summer that Pluto is no longer a planet. It is now a 'dwarf planet,' which is the scientific equivalent of being moved to the kids' table. I have taught nine planets for sixteen years. I have a mnemonic. I have a mobile hanging over lab station 4, hand-painted, with a tiny Pluto I made from a bead. A student asked today whether I was going to cut it down. I said no. I said science changes its mind when it gets better evidence, that this is the best thing about it, and that we should all be so brave. Then I went into the supply closet for a minute. Pluto stays on the mobile. He has a small asterisk now. I think it suits him. Homework: read section 2.3, and be kind to small things. — Mr. H

blog.title: Sir Isaac Newt Is Missing (UPDATE: Found)
blog.body: At 2:40 PM today, during the density lab, a student (who shall remain nameless, Derek) left the lid of the tank ajar. At 2:55 I counted zero newts. A newt, for those unfamiliar, is four inches of pure decision-making. We formed a search grid. Tim took the supply shelves. Gina brought out a device she said detects 'presences,' which I am fairly sure is a stud finder; it found two studs. The custodian, Mr. Ray, was very calm, which leads me to believe this is not his first newt. At 4:10, alone in the room, I heard a small sound behind the radiator. There he was, sitting on a lost pencil like a king on a log. I said, 'You scared me.' He said nothing, being a newt. But I want it on the record that in sixteen years of teaching, the only thing that has ever made me skip the pun of the day was that empty tank. He is home. The lid has a brick on it now. — Mr. H

survey.title: A Survey a Student Left on My Desk (I Believe as a Joke) (I Completed It)
qa: Name?
Mr. Henderson. I do have a first name. It is on my mug and nowhere else.
Favorite element?
Tungsten. Highest melting point, a symbol that makes no sense (W), deeply underrated. I relate.
What is in your pockets right now?
A green pen, a magnet, two granola bars, and a note that says 'newt food.'
Have you ever blown anything up?
On purpose, twice a year, behind the gym, with a permit. By accident, once. We do not talk about the ceiling tile.
Favorite pun?
That would be like choosing among my children. All 117 of them.
What did you want to be when you grew up?
An astronaut. Then I met ninth graders and realized I prefer my hostile environments with gravity.
Biggest fear?
An unlabeled beaker. Also that someday a student will ask 'when will I ever use this' and I will not have an answer ready. So far, I always have.
What did you do last weekend?
Graded 94 lab reports, turned the compost, and took Mrs. Henderson to the natural history museum. She chose the restaurant. That was the deal.
How many friends do you have on here?
Five. The trend line is flat, but it is not negative.
Coke or Pepsi?
Either, with a roll of mints, outdoors, standing well back.
Describe yourself in three words.
'Shows his work.'
Did you correct the grammar on this survey?
Yes. In green. Question 4 originally said 'blowed.'
